name: ERROR.TYPE

args.name: error_val
args.about: the error, or the cell holding it

about: Gives a number for which kind of error a value is.

example.why: C2 holds #DIV/0!, which is error number 2 (#NULL! is 1, #VALUE! 3, #REF! 4, #NAME? 5, #NUM! 6, #N/A 7).

notes: Gives #N/A when the value is not an error.

name: FORMULATEXT

args.name: reference
args.about: the cell whose formula to show

about: Shows the formula in a cell as text.

example.why: C2 holds the formula =A2*B2, shown here as text.

notes: Gives #N/A when the cell holds no formula.

name: ISBLANK

args.name: value
args.about: the cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a cell is empty.

example.why: Ann's phone cell has nothing in it.

notes: A cell with a formula giving "" is not blank.

name: ISERR

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is any error except #N/A.

example.why: Dividing by 0 gives #DIV/0!, which is an error other than #N/A.

notes: ISERROR also counts #N/A; ISNA counts only #N/A.

name: ISERROR

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is any error.

example.why: There is no Plum, so MATCH gives #N/A, which is an error.

notes: IFERROR shows something else in place of the error.

name: ISEVEN

args.name: number
args.about: the number to check; any fraction is dropped

about: Gives TRUE when a number is even.

example.why: 12 divides by 2 with nothing left over.

name: ISFORMULA

args.name: reference
args.about: the cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a cell holds a formula.

example.why: C2 is worked out by the formula =A2*B2 rather than typed in.

name: ISLOGICAL

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is TRUE or FALSE.

example.why: B2 holds the logical value FALSE.

name: ISNA

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is the #N/A error.

example.why: Plum isn't in the list, so MATCH gives #N/A.

notes: IFNA shows something else in place of #N/A.

name: ISNONTEXT

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is not text, including empty cells.

example.why: B2 holds the number 120, not text.

name: ISNUMBER

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is a number (dates and times count as numbers).

example.why: B2 holds the number 120.

notes: Numbers typed as text, like "120" in quotes, are not numbers.

name: ISODD

args.name: number
args.about: the number to check; any fraction is dropped

about: Gives TRUE when a number is odd.

example.why: 12 is even, so it is not odd.

name: ISOMITTED

args.name: argument
args.about: a parameter name of the LAMBDA it is used in

about: Inside a LAMBDA, gives TRUE when a value was left out of the call.

example.why: The rate is left out of the call, so the default of 20% is added: 50 × 1.2 = 60.

name: ISREF

args.name: value
args.about: the value to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is a cell or range reference.

example.why: B2 is a reference to a cell, whatever it holds.

name: ISTEXT

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives TRUE when a value is text.

example.why: A2 holds the word Lamp.

name: NA
about: Gives the #N/A error, to mark a value as missing.

example.why: It always gives #N/A, which charts skip and ISNA picks up.

name: SHEET

args.name: value
args.about: a sheet name in quotes (the formula's own sheet if left out)

about: Gives the number of a sheet, counting from the left.

example.why: Sheet1 is the first sheet from the left.

notes: Unlike some other spreadsheet apps, a cell reference like SHEET(B2) doesn't give that cell's sheet: the cell's contents are read as a sheet name, so it usually gives #N/A. Use the sheet's name in quotes instead.

name: TYPE

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to check

about: Gives a number for what kind of value something is: 1 number, 2 text, 4 logical, 16 error, 64 array.

example.why: A2 holds text, which is type 2.

name: SHEETS

args.name: reference
args.about: a reference whose sheets to count (the whole workbook if left out)

about: Gives how many sheets there are.

example.why: A new workbook has one sheet.

name: N

args.name: value
args.about: the value or cell to turn into a number

about: Turns a value into a number: numbers stay, TRUE is 1, text and FALSE are 0.

example.why: TRUE turns into 1.

name: CELL

args.name: info_type
args.about: what to find out, like "address", "row", "col", "contents" or "type"

args.name: reference
args.about: the cell to look at (the formula's own cell if left out)

about: Gives a fact about a cell, such as its address, row or what it holds.

example.why: The address of B2, written with dollar signs.

notes: "type" gives b for blank, l for text and v for anything else. "color", "format", "parentheses", "prefix", "protect" and "width" aren't worked out yet and give an error.

name: INFO

args.name: type_text
args.about: what to find out, like "numfile", "recalc" or "system"

about: Gives a fact about the workbook or the computer it is running on.

example.why: "numfile" gives how many sheets the workbook has.

notes: "directory", "origin" and "osversion" aren't worked out and give an error.
